By Adv. Sri.M.S.Sajeev Kumar Respondent(S): ------------------------- 1. The Commissioner Of Customs, Custom House, Willingdon Island, Cochin-682009. 2. Exhibit P2- True Copy Of The Packing List. Exhibit P3- True Copy Of The Certificate Of Origin With Reference No. Co/Isfta/13/10098. Exhibit P4- True Copy Of The Phytosanitary Certificate No. Qc/1A-0533091 Dated 29-11-2013. Exhibit P5- True Copy Of The Certificate Of Fumigation No. Sca/Ind/21499 Dated 25-11-2013. Exhibit P6- True Copy Of The Bill Of Entry No. 4064135 Dated 12-12-2013. Exhibit P7, P-7(A)- True Copy Of The Rejection Report Dated 03-1-2014 Along With Analysis Report Dated 1-1-2014. Exhibit P8- True Copy Of The Examination Order Dated 09-01-2014. Exhibit P9- True Copy Of The Release Order Dated 13/5/14 Respondent(S)' Exhibits ---------------------------------------
texts.facts: The facts involved in the above case would disclose that the petitioner imported 132 bags of fermented and dried Coco Beans and certain other items under Ext.P6 Bill of Entry. The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI), on inspection, found that coco beans were contaminated with fungal growth. As per the prescribed standards, the materials should be free from fungus. Ext.P7 is the report of the FSSAI which was communicated to the petitioner as well. According to the petitioner, after necessary fumigation, the fungal growth would be wiped off and there is no reason for detaining the goods. 3. In fact, pursuant to Ext.P7, the goods were not permitted to be released to the petitioner and it will be either confiscated or destroyed or necessary permission would be granted to re-export the materials, if it is permissible as per the procedure prescribed. 5. Petitioner subsequently produced Ext.P9 to indicate that the Director of Plant Protection, Quarantine & Storage Department, Government of India has issued certificate dated 13/05/2014 M/S.St.George Industries vs The Commissioner Of Customs on 28 November, 2013 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/26595297/ 3 indicating that the consignment has `passed'.
